title: Certificates of Deposit: when a maximum in-term add-on is not accepted at all
content:
## Scope

When the owner of a Certificates of Deposit certificate asks to move as much as the certificate will take into it as an in-term add-on, this rule states when the add-on sized for the request is accepted and when nothing is accepted.

## Rule

1. **Acceptance.** The add-on is accepted at its size only where the certificate can take an in-term add-on at all, the term's count of add-ons is not used up, and the size reaches the tier's smallest in-term add-on.
2. **Below the minimum.** When the size is below the tier's smallest in-term add-on, no add-on is accepted and nothing is written.
3. **Count used up.** When the count of add-ons in the term is used up, no add-on is accepted and nothing is written.
4. **Concentration cap.** The add-on must also keep the customer's total certificate principal within the customer-level concentration cap, which declines an add-on that would breach it rather than reducing it.

## Decision table

| Certificate can take an in-term add-on | Term count used up | Size at least the smallest in-term add-on | Within the concentration cap | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | No | Yes | Yes | Accepted at its size |
| Yes | No | No | Any | Nothing accepted, nothing written |
| Yes | Yes | Any | Any | Nothing accepted, nothing written |
| No | Any | Any | Any | Nothing accepted, nothing written |
| Yes | No | Yes | No | Declined in full, not reduced |

## Cases (illustrative smallest add-on of 50.00, not a tier value)

- The smallest room works out at 49.99. It is below 50.00, so nothing is accepted; the add-on is not raised to 50.00.
- The smallest room works out at 50.00. It meets the minimum, so 50.00 is accepted, subject to the concentration cap.
- The term's single add-on has already been made. Nothing is accepted, whatever the rooms.

## Points of judgement

**The concentration cap would be breached by the full size. Is the add-on cut back to fit the cap?**
No. The concentration cap declines an add-on that would breach it rather than reducing it.
